label: late encoding/<DEL> steps of sequences starting with w/d/e/u/c/0/q/b
explanation: Fires almost only during the original phase from t>=3 and at the <DEL> step: 92% of activation mass, but precision there is just 0.12. It never fires at t=0-1 and is weak in the copy phase (6% of mass). The rate rises with orig_idx (4x lift at positions 7-8) and with L. Whether it fires depends mostly on which tokens came early in the sequence. First token w/d/e/u/0/c gives 2.2-3.2x lift, and the second token from the same set also helps; top examples start w w, w d, w 0. The current input token matters a little (r/p/y/1/2 and first occurrences fire more). It acts like a graded accumulation of an early-token set rather than a clean rule: the first-token predicate gets F1 about 0.41 on dev, and OR-ing in the second token raises mass recall to 0.85 but cuts precision to 0.23. Magnitude was not separately modelled beyond the higher rate later in the sequence.
